abstract: Di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) is a ubiquitous environmental contaminant that has been implicated in immune and inflammatory dysregulation, but its potential role in psoriasis-related skin inflammation remains unclear. In this study, we integrated bioinformatics, network toxicology, and machine-learning analyses to identify candidate genes associated with DEHP-exacerbated psoriasis-like inflammation, followed by experimental validation in in vivo and in vitro models. Public transcriptomic datasets were analyzed to screen differentially expressed genes and prioritize key candidates. S100A9 and FABP5 were identified as high-priority genes by machine learning and were further examined in an imiquimod (IMQ)-induced psoriasis-like mouse model and in DEHP-treated HaCaT keratinocytes. Our results showed that DEHP exposure exacerbated IMQ-induced psoriasiform skin inflammation in mice and was associated with increased expression of S100A9, FABP5, and IL-17A-related inflammatory markers in mouse skin. In HaCaT cells, DEHP treatment was also associated with increased S100A9/FABP5 expression under the tested conditions. These exploratory findings suggest that DEHP exposure may exacerbate psoriasis-like skin inflammation and is associated with increased keratinocyte S100A9/FABP5 expression and IL-17A-related signaling. Translation to human psoriasis remains uncertain. Further functional studies are needed to clarify the causal role and mechanistic significance of this pathway.
